rationale: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence and keeping track of counted items in a scattered or unorganized set, resulting in counting some objects twice and skipping others. A structured ten-frame provides discrete, fixed physical slots so the student places one counter per slot while counting, visually anchoring exactly one number word to each object.
intent: Focus on the 'build' mode where the student places counters one by one into the 2x5 grid up to target quantities between 4 and 7 (avoiding 8, the current problem's count). Emphasize touching each space once as each number is counted so no counter is counted twice or missed.

data.title: Counting Objects to 10
data.description: Place counters into a ten-frame one at a time while counting to maintain one-to-one correspondence.

challenges.hint: Touch each space as you place 4 counters one by one.
challenges.narration: Let's build a group of 4 counters on the frame. Remember to place them one at a time!
challenges.instruction: Put 4 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row completely to make 5.
challenges.narration: Can you put 5 counters on the frame? Fill the top row first!
challenges.instruction: Put 5 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Let's practice 5 again to make sure we count carefully.
challenges.narration: Let's place 5 counters on the frame again, one by one.
challenges.instruction: Put 5 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Put 5 on the top row, and just 1 more on the bottom row.
challenges.narration: Now let's build 6 counters. That's a full top row and one more on the bottom.
challenges.instruction: Put 6 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.narration: Let's build 6 counters on the frame one more time.
challenges.instruction: Put 6 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row of 5, then add 2 more on the bottom.
challenges.narration: Can you place 7 counters on the frame? Take your time counting each one.
challenges.instruction: Put 7 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Check your work by pointing to each of the 7 counters.
challenges.narration: Great job! Let's do one final challenge and build 7 counters carefully.
challenges.instruction: Put 7 counters on the ten frame!

judgement.reasoning: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence and keeping track (counting objects twice or skipping). Using a ten-frame 'build' mode forces 1-to-1 placement into explicit discrete boxes (one counter per box), which directly scaffolds keeping track and preventing double-counting. The numbers (4-7) are simpler than 8, avoiding the failed item while practising the exact missing skill with a structured spatial manipulative.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would immediately use this structured ten-frame build activity to anchor one-to-one correspondence and physical tracking.
